library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib"))$description`
* Article: [Clin Pharmacol Ther 2026;120:753-761](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70367) (open access)

Tachet et al. followed adults treated with the JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor ruxolitinib
in routine Swiss practice and fitted a population PK model in Monolix to 221
steady-state concentrations, most of them single random samples taken at
outpatient visits. The final model is one-compartmental with first-order
absorption (ka fixed at 3.24 1/h) and linear elimination, with between-subject
variability on apparent clearance only. Body weight scales V/F linearly, and a
strong CYP3A or dual CYP2C9/CYP3A inhibitor (posaconazole, fluconazole) lowers
CL/F by 39%.

The paper then predicted each patient's steady-state trough (Cmin), peak (Cmax)
and daily AUC (AUC24) at every documented visit and related them to the
occurrence of any adverse event with univariable logistic regressions on the
log scale. Cmin and AUC24 were significant; Cmax was not (P = 0.25). The
package therefore carries three models from this paper:

| Model | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib` | Population PK model (Table 2) |
| `Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_ctrough` | Probability of any adverse event vs. steady-state Cmin (OR 1.51 per doubling) |
| `Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_auc24` | Probability of any adverse event vs. steady-state AUC24 (OR 1.88 per doubling) |

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib"))$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = c("Subjects", "Observations", "Age", "Body weight", "Height", "Female (%)",
            "Disease", "Dosing", "Co-medication", "Region"),
  Value = c(pop$n_subjects, pop$n_observations, pop$age_range, pop$weight_range,
            pop$height_range, pop$sex_female_pct, pop$disease_state, pop$dose_range,
            pop$co_medication, pop$regions)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Study population (Tachet 2026 Table 1 and Supplementary Table S2).")
```

The cohort was heterogeneous: graft-versus-host disease (43%) and
myeloproliferative neoplasms (about half, mostly myelofibrosis and polycythaemia
vera) dominate, with a few patients with VEXAS, APECED or haemophagocytic
lymphohistiocytosis. Eleven patients contributed a rich profile (pre-dose plus
seven samples over 8 h); the rest contributed one to eleven sparse samples.
Ruxolitinib regimens ranged from 5 mg once daily to 25 mg twice daily, with
some asymmetric and extended-interval schedules.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-compartment, first-order absorption, linear elimination | -- | Results, 'Structural, statistical, and covariate models' |
| `lka` | log(3.24) 1/h, fixed | Table 2 'k a (h-1)' = 3.24 FIX |
| `lvc` | log(69) L at 73 kg | Table 2 'V pop (L)' = 69 |
| `lcl` | log(14) L/h | Table 2 'CLpop' = 14 (unit misprinted as L) |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Table 2 'beta V,BW' = 1 FIX; footnote BWmedian = 73 kg |
| `e_conmed_cyp3a4_inh_strong_cl` | -0.50 | Table 2 'beta CL,CYP3A/2C9 inhibitors'; Results: 39% reduction |
| `etalcl` | 0.12825 = log(1 + 0.37^2) | Table 2 'omega CL (CV, %)' = 37 |
| `propSd` | 0.42 | Table 2 'sigma prop (CV, %)' = 42 |
| V/F equation | 69 * (WT/73)^1 | Table 2 footnote, 'Final model' |
| CL/F equation | 14 * exp(-0.50 * INH + eta) | Table 2 footnote, 'Final model' |
| `e_ctrough_logit` | log(1.51) per doubling of Cmin | Results, 'Exploratory PK/PD analysis' |
| `e_auc_ruxolitinib_logit` | log(1.88) per doubling of AUC24 | Results, 'Exploratory PK/PD analysis' |
| `logit_ref` (Cmin model) | -2.40 | Not printed; reconstructed from Figure 3 (below) |
| `logit_ref` (AUC24 model) | -7.53 | Not printed; reconstructed from Figure 3 (below) |
| Validation targets | Median Cmin, PI90, % above 21 ng/mL per regimen | Table 3; Figure 2; Results, 'Model-based simulations' |

# Typical-value checks

The paper reports that its model implies a Tmax of 0.92 h and a half-life of
3.45 h. The steady-state trough of a one-compartment model with first-order
absorption also has a closed form, which the ODE solution must reproduce to
numerical precision.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib")
ka <- 3.24; cl <- 14; vc <- 69
kel <- cl / vc
tmax <- log(ka / kel) / (ka - kel)
thalf <- log(2) / kel
stopifnot(abs(tmax / 0.92 - 1) < 0.02, abs(thalf / 3.45 - 1) < 0.02)

# Steady-state 10 mg twice daily, typical 73 kg patient without inhibitor
tau <- 12; dose <- 10
ev_typ <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = dose, ii = tau, ss = 1, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, tau, by = 0.25), evid = 0, amt = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0, cmt = "central")
)
ev_typ$WT <- 73
ev_typ$CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_STRONG <- 0
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
closed <- function(t) {
  1000 * dose * ka / (vc * (ka - kel)) *
    (exp(-kel * t) / (1 - exp(-kel * tau)) - exp(-ka * t) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))
}
err <- max(abs(sim_typ$Cc - closed(sim_typ$time)) / closed(sim_typ$time))
stopifnot(err < 1e-4)
tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Tmax (h)", "Half-life (h)", "Cmin at 10 mg BID, typical patient (ng/mL)",
               "Max relative error, ODE vs closed form"),
  Model = c(format(round(tmax, 2)), format(round(thalf, 2)), format(round(closed(tau), 1)),
            format(signif(err, 2))),
  Paper = c("0.92", "3.45", "--", "--")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value quantities of the final model.")
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation (Table 3, Figure 2)

The paper simulated steady state for 5-25 mg twice daily, with and without a
strong CYP3A or dual CYP2C9/CYP3A inhibitor, drawing body weight from a uniform
distribution over the study range (40.7-116 kg). The same design is used here
with 200 virtual patients per arm.

```{r simulate}
arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25), inh = c(0, 1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    arm = seq_len(dplyr::n()),
    treatment = sprintf("%d mg BID %s", dose, ifelse(inh == 1, "+ inhibitor", "alone"))
  )
n_per_arm <- 200
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261114)
set.seed(20261114)
subj <- arms[rep(seq_len(nrow(arms)), each = n_per_arm), ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = seq_len(dplyr::n()), WT = runif(dplyr::n(), 40.7, 116))
obs_times <- seq(0, tau, by = 0.25)
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  subj |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, ii = tau, ss = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  subj[rep(seq_len(nrow(subj)), each = length(obs_times)), ] |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = rep(obs_times, nrow(subj)), evid = 0L, amt = 0, ii = 0, ss = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_STRONG = inh) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, ii, ss, cmt, WT, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_STRONG, treatment, dose, inh)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = c("treatment", "dose", "inh"), returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc), length(unique(sim$id)) == nrow(subj))
```

## Table 3: trough concentrations

```{r table-3}
published_t3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~inh, ~med, ~lo, ~hi, ~pct21,
  5,  0, 7.5, 0.8, 28.0, 11,
  5,  1, 23,  6,   61,   55,
  10, 0, 16,  2,   55,   39,
  10, 1, 48,  11,  119,  85,
  15, 0, 25,  2,   87,   56,
  15, 1, 69,  18,  174,  94,
  20, 0, 32,  3,   118,  65,
  20, 1, 94,  22,  235,  95,
  25, 0, 39,  4,   130,  74,
  25, 1, 115, 24,  298,  96
)
cmin_sim <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == tau) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, inh) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_med = median(Cc), sim_lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), sim_hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    sim_pct21 = 100 * mean(Cc > 21), .groups = "drop"
  )
t3 <- dplyr::left_join(published_t3, cmin_sim, by = c("dose", "inh")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_med / med - 1))
t3 |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Regimen = paste(dose, "mg BID"), Inhibitor = ifelse(inh == 1, "+", "-"),
    `Median Cmin, paper` = med, `Median Cmin, model` = round(sim_med, 1),
    `PI90, paper` = sprintf("%g-%g", lo, hi),
    `PI90, model` = sprintf("%.1f-%.0f", sim_lo, sim_hi),
    `% > 21 ng/mL, paper` = pct21, `% > 21 ng/mL, model` = round(sim_pct21)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Tachet 2026 (model: 200 virtual patients per arm).")

stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed CL, V or inhibitor effect moves every arm by tens of percent.
  abs(median(t3$pct_diff)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(t3$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25,
  median(abs(t3$sim_pct21 - t3$pct21)) < 8
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Steady-state NCA over one 12 h interval at 10 mg twice daily. Figure 2 of the
paper labels its AUC panel 'AUC24', but its medians (about 715 and 1180
ng*h/mL, read from the figure) equal one 10 mg dose divided by CL/F (714 and
1177 ng*h/mL), i.e. the AUC over a 12 h dosing interval, so the interval AUC is
compared with them here.

```{r pknca}
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, dose == 10) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = tau, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                ~cmin, ~auclast,
  "10 mg BID alone",         16,    715,
  "10 mg BID + inhibitor",   48,    1180
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmin = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated medians vs. Table 3 (Cmin) and Figure 2 (interval AUC). * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

```{r pknca-ratios}
nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = med) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = `10 mg BID + inhibitor` / `10 mg BID alone`)
ratio_tab <- dplyr::left_join(
  nca_med,
  tibble::tibble(PPTESTCD = c("cmin", "auclast", "cmax"), paper = c(2.9, 1.7, 1.3)),
  by = "PPTESTCD"
)
ratio_tab |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    `NCA parameter` = c(auclast = "AUC0-12", cmax = "Cmax", cmin = "Cmin")[PPTESTCD],
    `Median ratio, model` = round(ratio, 2), `Median ratio, paper` = paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fold-increase of median exposure with a strong or dual inhibitor at 10 mg BID (Results, 'Model-based simulations').")
# AUC and Cmax ratios are close to deterministic (AUC: exactly exp(0.50) = 1.65
# for every subject); the Cmin ratio is a ratio of two cohort medians of a
# highly variable trough and carries about 10% Monte Carlo noise at 200 per arm.
tol <- c(auclast = 0.10, cmax = 0.10, cmin = 0.25)[ratio_tab$PPTESTCD]
stopifnot(all(abs(ratio_tab$ratio / ratio_tab$paper - 1) < tol))
```

# Exposure-toxicity models

## Reconstructing the unprinted intercepts

The paper prints each odds ratio (per two-fold increase in exposure) but not
the regression intercept. For a logistic regression fitted by maximum
likelihood, the fitted probabilities sum to the number of events. The
maintainers therefore reconstructed the visit-level exposure distribution from
Figure 3 and solved that score equation for the intercept, holding the slope at
its printed value:

* Box quartiles were read from the pixel rows of the box lines in Figure 3
  (axis calibrated from the tick marks).
* Within each group, log-exposure was represented by a split normal distribution
  that honours the first quartile, median and third quartile exactly.
* About 66 non-toxic and 31 toxic visits are plotted in Figure 3 (maintainers'
  count of the jittered points; overlapping points make the count uncertain by a
  few in each group).

```{r intercept}
fig3 <- list(
  ctrough = list(nt = c(4.79, 12.71, 25.21), t = c(9.38, 25.21, 48.54), or2 = 1.51),
  auc24   = list(nt = c(890.9, 1464.1, 2355.0), t = c(1180.9, 2313.5, 3031.8), or2 = 1.88)
)
u <- stats::ppoints(4000) # quadrature grid on (0, 1), not a cohort
split_normal_log <- function(q) {
  l <- log(q)
  ifelse(u < 0.5,
         l[2] + qnorm(u) * (l[2] - l[1]) / qnorm(0.75),
         l[2] + qnorm(u) * (l[3] - l[2]) / qnorm(0.75))
}
solve_intercept <- function(g, n0, n1) {
  b <- log(g$or2) / log(2)
  x0 <- split_normal_log(g$nt); x1 <- split_normal_log(g$t)
  uniroot(function(a) n0 * mean(plogis(a + b * x0)) + n1 * mean(plogis(a + b * x1)) - n1,
          c(-30, 30), tol = 1e-8)$root
}
counts <- list(c(66, 31), c(72, 29), c(60, 33))
recon <- do.call(rbind, lapply(counts, function(n) {
  data.frame(
    `Non-toxic n` = n[1], `Toxic n` = n[2],
    `Cmin model intercept` = round(solve_intercept(fig3$ctrough, n[1], n[2]), 3),
    `AUC24 model intercept` = round(solve_intercept(fig3$auc24, n[1], n[2]), 3),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(recon, caption = "Score-equation intercepts; first row is the central count, the others bracket it.")

ini_ref <- function(name) {
  ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(name))
  ui$iniDf$est[ui$iniDf$name == "logit_ref"]
}
stopifnot(
  abs(ini_ref("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_ctrough") - recon[1, 3]) < 0.01,
  abs(ini_ref("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_auc24") - recon[1, 4]) < 0.01
)
```

The count uncertainty moves each intercept by about 0.16 on the logit scale.
Using the auto-detected Figure 3 points directly instead of the split-normal
reconstruction gave -2.41 and -7.35, so the shipped values (-2.40 and -7.53)
are stable to the choice of reconstruction within about 0.2 logit.

## The packaged models reproduce the printed odds ratios

```{r er-check}
er_at <- function(model, covariate, value) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_along(value), time = 0)
  ev[[covariate]] <- value
  # The logistic models carry no random effect, so rxode2 notes that a
  # multi-subject solve has no omega; that is expected here.
  out <- withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(model), events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
  if (!is.null(out$id)) out <- out[order(out$id), , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == length(value))
  out$prob_ae
}
odds <- function(p) p / (1 - p)
p_c <- er_at("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_ctrough", "CTROUGH", c(10, 20))
p_a <- er_at("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_auc24", "AUC_RUXOLITINIB", c(1500, 3000))
or_c <- odds(p_c[2]) / odds(p_c[1])
or_a <- odds(p_a[2]) / odds(p_a[1])
stopifnot(abs(or_c - 1.51) < 1e-8, abs(or_a - 1.88) < 1e-8)
tibble::tibble(
  Model = c("Cmin", "AUC24"),
  `OR per doubling, model` = round(c(or_c, or_a), 4),
  `OR per doubling, paper` = c(1.51, 1.88)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Odds ratio per two-fold exposure increase (Results, 'Exploratory PK/PD analysis').")
```

## Probability of an adverse event across the simulated 10 mg BID cohort

```{r er-cohort}
ex <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmin", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc24 = 2 * auclast) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id)
ex$p_cmin <- er_at("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_ctrough", "CTROUGH", ex$cmin)
ex$p_auc <- er_at("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_auc24", "AUC_RUXOLITINIB", ex$auc24)
ex |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median Cmin (ng/mL)` = round(median(cmin), 1),
    `Median AUC24 (ng*h/mL)` = round(median(auc24)),
    `Mean P(AE), Cmin model` = round(mean(p_cmin), 2),
    `Mean P(AE), AUC24 model` = round(mean(p_auc), 2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Arm = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model-predicted probability of any adverse event at a visit.")

curve <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(metric = "Cmin (ng/mL)", x = exp(seq(log(1), log(150), length.out = 100))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(p = er_at("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_ctrough", "CTROUGH", x)),
  tibble::tibble(metric = "AUC24 (ng*h/mL)", x = exp(seq(log(200), log(5000), length.out = 100))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(p = er_at("Tachet_2026_ruxolitinib_ae_auc24", "AUC_RUXOLITINIB", x))
)
ggplot(curve, aes(x, p)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Steady-state exposure (log scale)", y = "P(any adverse event)",
       caption = "Exposure-toxicity relationships behind Figure 3 of Tachet 2026.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Intercepts of the exposure-toxicity models are reconstructed, not
  published.** The paper prints only the odds ratios. The intercepts come from
  the score equation over the Figure 3 exposure distributions with the printed
  slopes held fixed (see above). A free two-parameter fit to the reconstructed
  data gives shallower slopes (odds ratios about 1.3-1.4 for Cmin and 1.4-1.5
  for AUC24) than printed, still inside the published 95% confidence intervals;
  the printed slopes were kept. Treat absolute probabilities from these two
  models as approximate (about 0.2 logit).
* **Figure 2 'AUC24'** is the AUC over a 12 h dosing interval (its medians equal
  10 mg / CL/F), whereas the exposure-toxicity analysis and Figure 3 use a true
  24 h AUC (Figure 3 values reach 5000 ng*h/mL). The interval AUC is compared
  with Figure 2 here, and twice the interval AUC feeds the AUC24 model.
* **Reference body weight 73 kg** follows the Table 2 footnote and its model
  equation; Table 1 prints the patient-level median as 72.0 kg.
* **Between-subject variability on CL/F** is reported as a CV of 37% and
  converted to a log-normal variance, log(1 + 0.37^2) = 0.128. If the 37% were
  instead the Monolix omega (the standard deviation of eta), the variance would
  be 0.137; the difference is small.
* **Clearance unit**: Table 2 prints 'CLpop (L)'; the parameter is a clearance
  in L/h, consistent with the reported half-life.
* **Inhibitor category**: the indicator pools strong CYP3A inhibitors
  (posaconazole) and dual CYP2C9/CYP3A inhibitors (fluconazole), and leaves
  moderate CYP3A inhibitors and samples with missing status in the reference
  group, as the paper did.
* **Below-LLOQ data** (12 samples) were handled as censored in the source fit;
  this does not affect simulation.
* **Table 3 targets** come from 1,000 simulations in the paper; this vignette
  uses 200 virtual patients per arm, so its prediction-interval bounds carry
  more Monte Carlo noise than the medians.
* **Cmax** was tested in the exposure-toxicity analysis but not significant and
  no odds ratio is printed, so no Cmax model is packaged. The exposure-efficacy
  analysis (physician global assessment) found no significant relationship and
  printed no coefficients.
* No erratum was found for this article (checked 2026-11-14).
